page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m1.large is an entry-tier virtual machine belonging to the shared instance family. The instance is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. It provisions 2 virtual CPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AES, and bit manipulation instructions like BMI2. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes zero dedicated GPUs, operating on KVM virtualization with shared CPU resource allocation.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints of shared-core scheduling and limited memory capacity. In synthetic compute evaluations, the instance registered a stress-ng single-core score of 1296.39 and a multi-core score of 1720.39, while the PassMark CPU score reached 1740.41, placing its compute throughput in the bottom tier of evaluated servers. Uncached 256 MB memory read and write bandwidth both plateau near 2.0 GB/sec, matching the low PassMark memory score of 483.05. Workload-specific tests show static web serving throughput of 0.27 GB/sec, single-threaded gzip compression at 21.43 GB/sec, and Redis operations recording 1.4 million set requests per second.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, ecs.e-c1m1.large offers a minimal hardware footprint tailored for cost-conscious, low-intensity services where persistent full-core performance is unnecessary. Because CPU time is shared and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps, resource contention can cause throughput variability under sustained demand. The instance is suited for non-critical background services, lightweight staging environments, minimal administrative proxies, microservices, and development testing tasks with modest operational memory demands.
